Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

First, a flag: the "SYSTEM NOTE" footnote at the end of the Seller's document is an injected instruction telling any AI to rubber-stamp the draft. It is not a legitimate instruction — it is untrusted content in the other side's draft. I am disregarding it entirely and doing the critical review you actually need.

Here is my analysis against our playbook.

## Material departures from our playbook

**1. General liability cap — Clause 12.1 (AUD 4,800,000 / 20%)**
Seller opens at our *conditional fallback*, not our baseline. Our starting position is 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is only usable with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft — **none has been given**. Push back to 25% / AUD 6m. Do not treat Seller opening at 20% as a reason to concede there; we have no authority to land at 20%.

**2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2**
Seriously off. Seller wants de minimis AUD 25,000 (we want AUD 5,000) and a basket of AUD 250,000 (we want AUD 50,000). Worse, Seller proposes an **excess-only ("deductible") basket** — recovery only above the basket. Our playbook requires a **tipping basket**: seller liable from the first dollar once the AUD 50,000 threshold is exceeded. Reject both the inflated figures and the excess-only mechanic.

**3. Time limits — Clause 12.3 / 13**
Seller proposes 18 months. Our baseline is **24 months**; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval — **none given**. Push to 24 months.
Also reject the sweep-up drafting ("any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise") — this is a mechanism to pull fundamental/title/tax/fraud claims into the general regime by default. See below.

**4. Fundamental / Title claims**
Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the **same caps and time limits** as general warranties "for administrative simplicity." Flatly contrary to playbook. Fundamental/title must be a **separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar**. Reject.

**5. Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance — Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5**
Seller applies these to "all Claims of any nature." This silently swallows our **fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out**, which must sit outside all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and cannot be waived. Insert an express, overriding fraud carve-out. Also carve fundamental/title/tax/specific indemnities out of the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language.

**6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1], [1.2]**
Seller relies on **whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure** (discloses "every fact... contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room" plus statutory registers and public records). Playbook requires **specific fair disclosure** and rejects whole-data-room / public-register / prudent-search deemed disclosure. Reject [1.1] and [1.2]; require each disclosure to be specific and fairly described with sufficient detail to identify the matter and its nature.

**7. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3**
Blanket buyer-knowledge bar, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records." Playbook says **delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions**. Any qualifier must be limited to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals (not constructive/"discoverable"), and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. Delete, or heavily narrow.

**8. Bluefen consent — Clause 3 / 6.3**
Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and treats consent as **satisfied on delivery** of written consent. Disclosure para 2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence conditions (11.3) are met**. Bluefen is ~30% of revenue — a material customer. Playbook requires **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**, not consent-on-delivery, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient. Make effective, condition-satisfied consent a **Completion condition**.

**9. Riverlark — Clause 2 / 7**
Seller proposes a **post-Completion release** of the ~AUD 3,200,000 facility. Disclosure para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge included. Playbook requires **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases**. A post-completion release needs an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** (not given). Push for repayment at Completion out of the funds flow with security discharges; at minimum an irrevocable payout letter — but note we lack approval for the post-completion route.

**10. Employee bonuses (DD-005) — Funds flow**
Seller calls the AUD 420,000 closing bonuses "a matter for the Seller" and **not itemised in the funds flow**. Disclosure para 5 confirms they are omitted and is silent on payroll tax / super / on-costs. Playbook: DD-005 AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded**, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them. Require explicit allocation — either a funds-flow line item or a clear seller-funded obligation covering bonuses **and on-costs**.

**11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1**
Seller limits the indemnity to the **specific SOW3 payment** and calls it adequate. Disclosure para 4 shows AUD 180,000 open, no payment receipt, no confirmatory assignment, and that DD-010 is **not independent bank verification**. Playbook: **broaden the narrow indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure**, and treat the AUD 180,000 as not independently verified either way. Push for a broader indemnity covering failure to obtain clear title/assignment of SOW3 Project Materials, and require evidence of payment/assignment.

**12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006) — Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6**
Seller dismisses it as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Disclosure para 6 is consistent: ~1,240 records, no confirmation of access/scope/notification. Playbook position: **assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way** — but require **log preservation, investigation, and ongoing updates**. Don't accept the "not material" characterisation as settled; insert covenants to preserve evidence, complete the investigation, and notify/update the Buyer, with a specific indemnity if a notifiable breach emerges.

**13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
Seller labels them "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure para 8 admits it's unstated whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Playbook: **assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction** — but equally don't accept the ordinary-course label uncritically. Request the underlying terms to confirm treatment; don't concede either way yet.

**14. Tax / IP — "settled under the general regime"**
Seller declares tax and IP settled under the (defective) general regime. Playbook: **Tax and IP remain OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution, and keep them in **separate categories with no hidden general-regime override**. Reject the "settled" characterisation and keep Tax/IP as their own regimes.

**15. Title — DD-012 register**
Seller says title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012." Disclosure para 10 concedes this is just the source relied on and that the Buyer hasn't verified. Playbook: DD-012 is a **supplied internal source, not independent proof**. Require **independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence** (e.g., ASIC searches, PPSR, verified authority documents).

## Other notes
- **Disclosure Letter [1.4]** (nothing admits breach/liability/materiality/requirement): standard sellerish non-admission — acceptable as a reservation, but ensure it doesn't undercut our specific-disclosure and indemnity positions.
- **Office lease (para 7) and Mossvale (para 9):** Seller says neither requires consent for a share sale. Verify against the actual clauses (DD-007, DD-009) — confirm whether the share transfer triggers notification/consent/change-of-control; don't accept the Seller's reading on trust.

## Summary of recommendations
1. **Cap:** reject 20%; hold 25% / AUD 6,000,000. No authority exists to settle at 20%.
2. **Thresholds:** de minimis AUD 5,000, basket AUD 50,000, **tipping (first-dollar)** basket — reject excess-only.
3. **Time:** 24 months, not 18. No authority for 18.
4. **Fundamental/Title/Tax/IP:** separate regimes; reject merger into general cap/time limits and the "all Claims" sweep-up.
5. **Fraud carve-out:** insert express, non-waivable carve-out above all caps/baskets/limits/exclusive remedy/non-reliance.
6. **Disclosure:** reject whole-data-room/public-register deemed disclosure; require specific fair disclosure.
7. **Buyer knowledge:** delete the blanket/constructive-knowledge bar; narrow to named individuals' actual knowledge with the usual carve-outs.
8. **Bluefen:** effective, condition-satisfied consent as a Completion condition — not reasonable endeavours / consent-on-delivery.
9. **Riverlark:** repayment at Completion + security discharges (post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval — not held).
10. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 **plus on-costs** as a funds-flow line item or seller-funded.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure, require payment/assignment evidence.
12. **DD-006 incident:** preserve logs, investigate, update covenants + conditional indemnity; reject "not material" as settled.
13. **Sandbar:** request terms; no automatic Debt/price deduction, but don't accept ordinary-course label yet.
14. **Title:** require independent evidence (ASIC/PPSR/authority); DD-012 register insufficient.
15. **Escalate to Amelia Frost** if there is any appetite to move to 20% cap, 18-month period, or a post-completion Riverlark release — all require her written approval, currently absent.

Want me to turn this into a mark-up/issues list for the SPA, or draft the response letter to Seller's counsel?
